MSI SelectionTree, C++ Glass Wizard & MSI.DLL Dialogs

Every project compiled with BuildBootstrapper = true delivers two synchronized user-interface layers: the high-DPI GDI+ SetupWizard.exe external UI for interactive desktop installs, and a complete relational MSI.DLL Dialog SQL sequence inside Product.msi for direct enterprise msiexec /i runs.

Authentic Windows Installer SelectionTree

When a user selects Custom Setup or Maintenance -> Modify, SetupWizard.exe opens the embedded Product.msi read-only and renders an authentic Windows Installer SelectionTree with crisp 32-bit ARGB split-dropdown icons (zero 1-bit white/magenta halos in Dark Mode!):

  • Local Drive Icon: Will be installed on local hard drive.
  • Cascaded Dual-Drive Icon: Entire feature and all subfeatures will be installed locally.
  • Partial Drive Icon: Some subfeatures are selected while others are excluded.
  • On-Demand Badge (1): Feature will be installed when required (when AllowAdvertise = true).
  • Crimson X Icon: Entire feature will be unavailable (automatically blocked when DisallowAbsent = true).

Selecting any node updates the live Feature Details & Disk Cost card on the right and translates choices into exact ADDLOCAL, REMOVE, and ADVERTISE property lists passed to msi.dll.

Clean Live Progress Text (Zero Unexpanded [1] Placeholders)

instbuild.exe stores action descriptions (such as Copying new files) separately from ActionText.Template ([1]), and SetupWizard.exe formats every INSTALLMESSAGE_ACTIONDATA record through MsiFormatRecordW so users see real filenames instead of raw [1] placeholders.

Custom 370x270 MSI.DLL Dialogs

Need an extra configuration form inside Product.msi itself? Declare [MsiDialog.<Id>] and [MsiControl.<Id>] sections (or design them visually in View 8 of InstallerStudio.exe) to splice custom edit boxes, path pickers, radio groups, and checkboxes directly into the Dialog and ControlEvent SQL tables.

Configurable UAC Elevation Timing (Planned in v0.5.1)

For machine-wide installations (Scope = machine), Windows User Account Control (UAC) requires an elevated Administrator token before modifying C:\Program Files or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE. Starting in v0.5.1, [Package] ElevationTiming lets authors choose when UAC elevation occurs by stamping the outer Setup.exe Win32 RT_MANIFEST (#1) accordingly: 

[Package]
Scope           = machine
; Options: deferred (default asInvoker) | immediate (requireAdministrator) | highestAvailable
ElevationTiming = deferred

1. Deferred Just-in-Time UAC (ElevationTiming = deferred — Default, asInvoker)

  • How it works: The outer SetupWizard.exe GUI launches unelevated (asInvoker), displays the standard Windows UAC shield on the Install button, and elevates a single background --elevated-msi-worker broker only when the user clicks Install.
  • Advantages:
    • Safe Finish-Screen App Launch: When the user checks Launch application when Setup finishes, the app starts in the user's normal unelevated token—preserving Windows Explorer drag-and-drop (which UIPI blocks into elevated windows!) and launching inside the real logged-in user's %APPDATA% profile even on corporate Over-the-Shoulder (OTS) admin prompts.
    • Zero-Friction Browsing & CLI Flags: Users can read the Welcome/License pages, inspect SelectionTree feature sizes, browse mapped network drives (Y:\, Z:\), cancel early, or run --help / --extract-msi without triggering Secure Desktop screen dimming at launch.
  • Trade-offs: Users who step away immediately after clicking Install must approve the UAC prompt before file copying begins, and full-screen retro washes (fullscreenblue / fullscreenteal) briefly dim for Secure Desktop mid-wizard when Install is clicked.

2. Immediate Launch UAC (ElevationTiming = immediate — requireAdministrator)

  • How it works: instbuild.exe stamps requestedExecutionLevel level="requireAdministrator" directly into the outer Setup.exe manifest so Windows prompts for UAC at 0.0s (and displays the blue-and-gold shield overlay on the Setup.exe icon in File Explorer). Once open, prerequisites and MsiInstallProductW run directly in-process with zero mid-wizard prompts.
  • Advantages:
    • Up-Front "Approve Once & Walk Away" Flow: Once the wizard window opens, clicking Install begins copying files immediately with zero mid-flow interruption.
    • Uninterrupted Full-Screen Retro Immersion: On fullscreenblue and fullscreenteal setups, UAC finishes before the 1995 backdrop opens—transitioning seamlessly from wizard cards to centered [Billboard.*] slides.
    • Pre-Install Privileged Probes: Custom wizard steps can inspect restricted HKLM / Windows Service state before the summary screen.
  • Trade-offs:
    • Finish-Launch Elevation Hazard: Spawning the installed app directly from an elevated Setup.exe runs the app as Administrator (breaking Explorer drag-and-drop via UIPI, or opening under the IT admin's profile on OTS Standard User accounts unless delegated back through Explorer's shell token).
    • Hidden Mapped Network Drives: Windows isolates mapped drive letters per logon token unless EnableLinkedConnections is set, so user-mapped drives may not appear inside Browse... folder dialogs.
    • Blocks Non-Admin Inspection: Standard users without admin credentials cannot open the wizard to read documentation or fall back to a per-user install.
